limitations: Lean defines stability by the Routh-Hurwitz sign test (trace<0, det>0); it does NOT prove the eigenvalue equivalence, real eigenvalues/IVT, or any PDE or biological statement. Python numpy eigvals is a floating-point cross-check on n<=2000 only; modes beyond are covered by the analytic tail rule (Lean neumann_tail_hurwitz).
Adapter-added domain choice: 1-D zero-flux Neumann interval; Turing's own finite-domain discussion is a ring. Periodic/Dirichlet are refused, not supported.
Wavelength gate thresholds (near-onset tolerance, domain/lambda multiple) are requester-declared; the Delphi record gives none.
Fixed point and Jacobian are declared, not verified; J is a hand-picked illustration, not fitted to any system.
Delphi records are local unsigned nanopubs; no network nanopub ID exists or is claimed. Adapter reviewed by the authoring model only, not an independent human.
claim_runtime is absent from this branch so the module has its own small loader (hash convention verified compatible); an integrator may later swap in claim_runtime.common.

Site shows recorded Python outputs; only L=pi and L=2pi carry full mode tables, other lengths show recorded scan verdicts. Not computed in browser. Light/dark CSS present; only light mode was screenshotted.
No novelty, prospective, wet-lab or nanofabrication claim. Finite-domain Turing analysis is classical.
